findings.claim: The course intake's Concept-day allocation for S20 (authoring/evidence/html-css-js/intake.md, section Block allocation per day) schedules topic videos only in the 8-minute Short video block, 'topic videos whose runtimes sum to 8 minutes or less across the day (a video that does not fit is recorded absent with the reason)'. The four S20 companions assign 7.30 (semantic), 2.22 (forms), 7.57 (accessibility) and 8.37 (box model) optional watch minutes, 25.46 minutes in all, so at most one or two of them fit the block. This 7.57-minute whole-video assignment alone nearly fills the block.
findings.recommendation: If this video stays scheduled, assign only the part that serves o2 (the native button segment, 5:04 to 7:34, about 2.5 minutes) and say the earlier part is optional background; otherwise record the day-level choice and mark it unscheduled or absent per the intake.

findings.claim: The creator description carries no timestamp chapters and the player metadata exposes none, yet the companion says the coverage and its minute ranges come 'Per its chapters, description and captions' and the cautions say fit was judged from 'the chapters'. A learner or reviewer cannot tell where the segment boundaries come from.
findings.recommendation: Say where the time ranges come from (YouTube auto-generated key moments, or caption timestamps) and drop 'chapters' wherever the creator published none, in both the body line and the cautions.

findings.claim: The 3:30 to 5:04 range shows tabindex and JavaScript click and key handling on a div. S20 learners have not met JavaScript event handling yet (JavaScript starts on S22), and the page only describes a div with no key handler. The cautions do not tell a beginner that the code in this part is not something they need to write or follow, so a learner could take 'add key handlers' as the lesson instead of 'just use button'.
findings.recommendation: Add a caution such as: 'The middle part shows JavaScript key handlers on a div; you do not need to follow that code. The point, as on the page, is that a native button needs none of it.'
